text:
Mattias Samuelsson is playing more than ever: 23:44 a night this season and almost 25 minutes over his last ten games. Buffalo leans on him in every situation except the power play, and he's still producing, with 10 points in 17 games, all at even strength or shorthanded.

The big Philadelphia native is a throwback in some ways (6'4", 234 pounds, 35 blocked shots) but he moves better than he looks: his top skating speed and burst count both sit around the 90th percentile among players we track, and his shot reaches 94 mph.

Evolving-Hockey had him as one of the league's better defensemen last season, 2.4 wins above replacement and 20th among 215, which surprised people who think of him as a defensive defenseman. This year's on-ice numbers are more ordinary: Buffalo has 49.6% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, a little worse than without him. That's the thing to watch with this much ice time. Our range has him around 48 points, which would be a career year.
headline: Mattias Samuelsson is Buffalo's minutes-eater
